denkroutine.titel: Before every move: the thinking routine

schritte.text: What did your opponent's last move change, and what is the threat? Warning signs on both sides. Which phase? Then the tool from card 2.
First checks, captures, threats, yours and your opponent's. If nothing is forcing: the best quiet move with the tool of your phase. Two or three candidates.
For each candidate, the strongest reply, not the most convenient one. At least two replies deep; calculate every candidate to the end.
Calculate until the position is quiet, then count: material, king safety, activity. Choose the candidate that does best against the strongest reply.

sicherheitsblick.text: Is my king safe afterwards? Can my opponent capture the moved piece right away? Do I allow a check or mate?

lernziele.einleitung: Before you read on with Chapter 1, you should be able to do the following with confidence:
punkte: orient the board from White's point of view
move and capture legally with every piece
get out of check
tell stalemate from checkmate
name the conditions for castling
recognize en passant
read a short move sequence in algebraic notation and write one down yourself
know the rules at the tournament board and the ways a game can end in a draw

lernziele.einleitung: Before you read on with Chapter 2, you should be able to do the following with confidence:
punkte: check the three opening goals in a position
recognize the four deadly sins of the opening
ask the four questions of the Chess X-ray rule before every move
count the attackers and defenders on a contested square, together with their values
hold the tension until the exchange gets you something
count whether you have superior force before you attack

lernziele.einleitung: Bevor du mit Kapitel 3 weiterliest, solltest du Folgendes sicher können:
punkte: an einer Eröffnungsstellung die drei Prüfungen (Zentrum, Entwicklung, Königssicherheit) für beide Seiten durchführen
die Hauptvariante deiner drei Eröffnungen bis zur Schlussstellung aufs Brett bringen und sagen, was beide Seiten dort erreicht haben
die typischen Fehler deiner Eröffnungen erkennen, etwa 4... Sf6?? in der Russischen Verteidigung oder 5... Sxd5?! im Zweispringerspiel
eine bekannte Stellung auch nach einer Zugumstellung wiedererkennen
sagen, gegen welche gegnerischen Antworten du einen Plan brauchst

lernziele.einleitung: Before you read on with Chapter 4, you should be able to do the following with confidence:
punkte: recognize a pawn offer as a real sacrifice or a pseudo-sacrifice
draw up a factor balance for a position yourself, taking into account who is to move when you count time
play the defense against the gambits that hit your repertoire
give back an extra pawn at the right moment

lernziele.einleitung: Before you read on with Chapter 5, you should be able to do the following with confidence:
punkte: ask the three check questions before taking any material you are offered
recognize the five warning signs on the board
know the traps that hit your repertoire, both as the victim and as the trap-setter

lernziele.einleitung: Before you read on with Chapter 6, you should be able to do the following with confidence:
punkte: before each pawn move of your own, say which squares it gives up forever and which of the four reasons it fulfills
recognize holes, outposts and the danger in front of your own king
use the protection test to find doubled pawns, backward pawns, isolanis, hanging pawns and chain bases, and count the pawn islands
read from the direction of the chains, space and the majorities which wing you play on, and blockade an enemy passed pawn
recognize whether a position is open, half-open, closed or mobile, and decide whether to open it
use the skeleton X-ray to put a plan for an unfamiliar structure into one sentence and derive a first move from it

lernziele.einleitung: Before you read on with Chapter 7, you should be able to do the following with confidence:
punkte: say what counts now in a quiet position: king safety, activity and pawn structure
decide whether to play on a wing or in the center – depending on whether the center is closed or open and where the kings are
check the three conditions for a king attack with same-side castling
spot your opponent's plan from a concrete move and prevent it in advance
use the five defensive resources to take away one of the conditions of an attack already under way
fix a weakness, play against it and create a second one
find your least active piece and clear a path for it to the plan, for example a rook via the open file to the seventh rank
draw up a plan balance for both sides
judge an unequal trade and an exchange sacrifice with the factor balance
convert a material advantage with the right trades

lernziele.einleitung: Before you read on with Chapter 8, you should be able to do the following:
punkte: find the matching motif for every warning sign, for both sides
calculate several candidates one after another until the position is quiet, and draw up the balance
test a threat with the five defense questions
count an exchange on a square correctly, including pieces lined up one behind the other
recognize the mating patterns of this chapter
look for perpetual check and stalemate in a lost position

lernziele.einleitung: Before you read on with Chapter 9, you should be able to do the following:
punkte: deliver mate with queen and with rook confidently and without stalemate, the rook mate also from the middle of the board
recognize and use the opposition, also from a distance
determine a pawn's key squares and lead the king there
calculate the pawn endgame before trading the last piece
decide with the square rule and by counting whether a passed pawn gets through
create a passed pawn from a majority and use an outside passed pawn as a lure
hand over the right to move with triangulation or a spare tempo

lernziele.einleitung: Before you read on with Chapter 10, you should be able to do the following:
punkte: recognize whether a king is cut off, and tell the short side from the long side
set up the Philidor position and switch behind the pawn at the right moment
win the Lucena position: drive the king away, rook to the 4th rank, build a bridge
apply the Vancura idea against a rook's pawn and avoid the skewer on the 7th rank
assess rook against pawn by cutting off and counting
win queen against pawn without stalemate and keep perpetual check in mind in queen endgames
recognize the typical drawing patterns with bishops and the fortress

lernziele.einleitung: Before you read on with Chapter 11, you should be able to do the following:
punkte: solve a study with the tool's four additional checks
explain why only the rook wins in the Saavedra study
use the Réti idea to find a king route with two goals
block the path of an enemy piece with a sacrifice or a quiet move
check every piece one by one when you suspect stalemate, and recognize a stalemate reserve

lernziele.einleitung: Before you read on, you should be able to do the following:
punkte: name the tool a position calls for
play through a master game on the board and state the plan in one sentence at each diagram
explain why Colle's sacrifice needed the opponent's help and Lasker's did not
redo a factor balance when material is won back or sacrificed anew
say before a trade which pieces will remain
in rook endgames, ask about activity first and only then about material

lernziele.einleitung: Before you close the book, you should be able to do the following:
punkte: determine the phase of the game before a move, go through the four steps of the thinking routine and check at least two candidate moves along the way
analyze one of your own games without an engine first and enter the most important mistake in the mistake log
draw up a training plan for your level
divide your thinking time with checkpoints
